header_summary:
The integration of company-specific quantum-resistant cryptosystems (CQRC) into blockchain technology introduces significant complexities, particularly when implementing sunset forks that could potentially undermine chain finality due to economic incentives for reorganization by entities. Proposed solutions to mitigate these risks include the use of periodic checkpoints secured by PQ-safe public keys, aiming to limit the depth of reversible blockchain alterations and enhance security against coordinated attacks involving CQRCs and large mining coalitions [source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/CALZpt+EjD5h9387diQvwtUY9nV-GFgN-Ukp9tY=uqBofb-w7Tg@mail.gmail.com/T/#mc9248eb0264c89e1fdedbf4fd00e749184fe7918).

Significant advancements in the 'backbone' project have been achieved, with the 6th release enhancing quality assurance and testing phases, including successful integration of bitcoind's python functional tests. This version supports a multi-daemon process and has improved the functionality of backbone-cli for controlling the main daemon during tests, laying a robust foundation for further development and testing on Linux systems [source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/CALZpt+Ec=cmFmEesnQ4DKvux-aK80ZiMw30+N8ZGyxDU2tWvxg@mail.gmail.com/T/#u#mfbfd449a00f35bb3e6e5b78a1860efd8979a6379).

Bitcoin Core version 30.3 introduces various enhancements including performance improvements, bug fixes, and new features, with significant contributions from developers aiming to bolster the software’s infrastructure. The release is compatible with several operating systems and includes updates like corrections in the chainstate database to reduce disk operations, and improvements in transaction fee handling and coin selection [source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/c359b0af-ea71-4a8c-913a-da0e65b8aa29n@googroups.com/T/#u#md54f0ba29b583ece2d476cb9117024646b3661cd).

The implementation of BIP 360 (P2MR) in a regtest environment showcases a practical assessment and highlights areas for improvement in the specification's clarity. This implementation is a step towards refining Bitcoin's scripting capabilities, with feedback suggesting enhancements in documentation and testing vectors to ensure clearer guidelines for future implementations [source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/bip-360-p2mr-implemented-in-bitcoin-core-on-regtest-vector-results-measurements-spec-feedback/2751).

recent_posts.title: The game-theory problems of PQ sunsetting modes
recent_posts.summary:
- Implementing CQRCs in blockchains raises significant technical and incentive-related challenges.
- Mining strategies that favor revisionist chains pose risks like double-spending and transaction rollback.
- Proposed solutions include PQ-safe checkpoints to secure blockchain against economically driven reorganizations.

recent_posts.title: new backbone code release with bitcoind python test framework integration
recent_posts.summary:
- The 6th public release of the Backbone project enhances quality assurance and testing.
- Backbone's update successfully integrates bitcoind's Python tests for multi-daemon processes.
- Further improvements involve backbone-cli modifications and tests on Linux-only platforms.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core 30.3 released
recent_posts.summary:
- Bitcoin Core version 30.3 features enhancements, bug fixes, and system compatibility updates.
- Users can report issues via GitHub and should follow specific upgrading instructions for different operating systems.
- Significant updates include database fixes, improvements in wallet and transaction handling, and enhanced testing protocols.

recent_posts.title: BIP 360 (P2MR) implemented in Bitcoin Core on regtest: vector results, measurements, spec feedback
recent_posts.summary:
- The programmer implemented BIP 360 in a regtest environment to evaluate its feasibility.
- Implementation results were promising, identifying both strengths and areas needing refinement.
- Ongoing community collaboration aims to refine and potentially expand the application of BIP 360.

recent_posts.title: Onion Message Jamming in the Lightning Network
recent_posts.summary:
- Reputation systems in network nodes improve security and hold peers accountable.
- Rate limiting and reputation charges reduce risks and long-term attack impacts.
- The system balances security enhancements with operational and privacy challenges.

recent_posts.title: Does Bitcoin's fee market price permanence, or just congestion?
recent_posts.summary:
- Bitcoin's fee debate questions the lifetime data storage costs reflected by the network.
- Findings show an annual full node operational cost of roughly $925, with $0.008 per inscription.
- The fee market misaligns with recurrent, unchosen storage costs, pushing for protocol reassessment.

active_posts.title: BIP draft: CISA for Taproot Key Path Spends
active_posts.summary: - A new Bitcoin Improvement Proposal draft introduces cross-input signature aggregation.  - The proposal provides options for half-aggregation, full-aggregation, or opting out.  - Developers are encouraged to review and give feedback on the proposed system online.

active_posts.title: Quantum Recovery Of Hashed Address Secured Coins With No Confiscatory Risk
active_posts.summary:
- Quantum computing threats drive the need for quantum-safe cryptocurrency signatures.
- Various proposals address recovery and ownership verification for ECC-based scripts.
- These solutions, however, fail to fully protect non-hashed address types from quantum risks.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Informational BIP on Low-R Signature Grinding
active_posts.summary:
- The new Bitcoin Improvement Proposal formalizes the Low-R signature documentation.
- Developers enhanced the secp256k1-jdk in Java using existing C++ and Rust resources.
- Feedback is sought for the BIP, focusing on content and test vector sources.

active_posts.title: [BIP Draft] Segregated Data: a prunable, script-isolated block region for data carriage
active_posts.summary:
- SegData proposes efficient Bitcoin block data storage through a new soft-fork mechanism.
- It features prunable data entries, managed via distinct Merkle roots and coinbase outputs.
- The primary users are off-chain services like indexers and timestamping, excluding covenant-style data uses.

active_posts.title: Changes to BIP-360 - Pay to Quantum Resistant Hash (P2QRH)
active_posts.summary:
- Recent BIP-360 updates enhance Bitcoin's defense against quantum threats via P2QRH adjustments.
- These changes utilize taproot infrastructure, simplifying integration and boosting long-term security.
- A new plan separates Post-Quantum signature development from BIP-360, ensuring flexible future enhancements.

active_posts.title: Addressing the Diminishing Block Subsidy
active_posts.summary:
- The proposed 0.25 BTC per block tail emission starts in 2040 to stabilize miner revenue.
- Critics fear the potential alteration to the 21 million BTC cap could devalue Bitcoin.
- Alternatives like proof-of-stake were rejected, favoring a mining-based security budget.

today_in_history_posts.title: Smaller Transactions with PubRef
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- A new opcode in the BIP reduces transaction size by approximately 37%.
- Reduced data recording enhances transaction volume and accesses small values economically.
- The BIP's details are posted on GitHub; Ethereum has a similar transaction called Ditto.

- Rusty suggests adding `commit_switch` and `commit_switch_reply` for double-opt-in.

today_in_history_posts.summary:
